decisions.reason: The client confirms that the Hero V is working and must be preserved, but does not change its already established geometry or full-wordmark scope.
The second V is identified as working and as an approved element to retain; its existing hierarchy rules remain unchanged.
The literal copy-and-paste derivation is reiterated for preservation, but the candidate already requires exact reuse of the Hero V terminal geometry.
The source does not modify the established peak-alignment rule; its general instruction to preserve prior relationships leaves the candidate state unchanged.
The client confirms the second V is working but introduces no change to its derivation or right-arm geometry.
Requiring the approved accent relationship to carry forward is consistent with the existing shared-terminal treatment and does not alter its current attributes.
Presenting E and L concepts as complete wordmarks does not establish any new kerning or spacing rule.
The source concerns structural letterform evaluation and does not resume or change the deferred champagne material treatment.
The instruction to preserve prior decisions and evaluate one variable at a time does not change the separate obligation to provide design rationale with review rounds.
